n.17: Possibly said with irony: "so that it may become clear which of you are the approved ones". Greek *dokimoi*, "tested, approved".
n.18: Or "it is not possible to eat the Lord's Supper".
n.19: Or "each of you eats his own supper first".
n.20: "Received" and "handed on" are the usual words for passing on a tradition (as in 15:3). Compare Mark 14:22–24, Matthew 26:26–28 and Luke 22:19–20.
n.21: Or "betrayed". Greek *paradidomi*, the verb translated "handed on" earlier in the verse.
n.23: Many manuscripts read "which is broken for you".
n.25: Literally "will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord".
n.26: "The body" may be the Lord's body in the bread (verse 27), or the church as the body of Christ (10:17; 12:27), or both. Many manuscripts read "whoever eats and drinks in an unworthy manner" and "the body of the Lord".
n.27: Verses 29–34 play on words formed from *krino*, "judge": *krima*, "judgment" (verses 29 and 34), *diakrino*, "discern" (verses 29 and 31), and *katakrino*, "condemn" (verse 32).
n.29: Greek *diakrino*, the verb translated "discerning" in verse 29.
n.30: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike (see 1:10).

v: Now concerning spiritual gifts,[^1] brothers and sisters,[^2] I do not want you to be uninformed.
Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν.
You know that when you were Gentiles,[^3] you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.[^4]
οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι.
Therefore I want you to understand that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is cursed!"[^5] and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord!" except by the Holy Spirit.
διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει· Ἀνάθεμα Ἰησοῦς, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν· Κύριος Ἰησοῦς εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
There are different kinds of gifts,[^6] but the same Spirit;
Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα·
there are different kinds of service,[^7] and the same Lord;
καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς κύριος·
and there are different kinds of activities, but the same God, who works all of them in everyone.
καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς θεός, ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
To each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον.
To one is given through the Spirit a message of wisdom,[^8] to another a message of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα,
to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit,
ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ πνεύματι,

to another the working of miracles,[^9] to another prophecy,[^10] to another the ability to distinguish between spirits,[^11] to another various kinds of tongues,[^12] to another the interpretation of tongues.
ἄλλῳ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ἄλλῳ προφητεία, 1ἄλλῳ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, 2ἄλλῳ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν·
All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who distributes them to each one individually, just as he wills.
πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.
Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη πολλὰ ἔχει, πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός·
For in one Spirit[^13] we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν, εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες, εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ πάντες ἓν πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν.
For the body does not consist of one member but of many.
Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά.
If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body.
ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος;
And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body.
καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος·
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole body were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός, ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή; εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή, ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις;
But as it is, God has arranged the members in the body, each one of them, just as he wanted.
νυνὶ δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη, ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν.
If they were all one member, where would the body be?
εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος, ποῦ τὸ σῶμα;
As it is, there are many members, but one body.
νῦν δὲ πολλὰ μὲν μέλη, ἓν δὲ σῶμα.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί· Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν· Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω·
On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are all the more necessary,
ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν,
and the parts of the body that we think less honorable we clothe with greater honor, and our unpresentable parts[^14] are treated with greater modesty,
καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος, τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν, καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει,
which our presentable parts do not need. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ἔχει. ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα, τῷ ὑστεροῦντι περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν,
so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same concern for one another.
ἵνα μὴ ᾖ σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσι τὰ μέλη.
If one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; if a member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
καὶ εἴτε πάσχει ἓν μέλος, συμπάσχει πάντα τὰ μέλη· εἴτε δοξάζεται μέλος, συγχαίρει πάντα τὰ μέλη.
Now you are the body of Christ, and individually members of it.
Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους.
And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, forms of help, forms of guidance,[^15] and various kinds of tongues.
καὶ οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, ἔπειτα δυνάμεις, ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων, ἀντιλήμψεις, κυβερνήσεις, γένη γλωσσῶν.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?[^16]
μὴ πάντες ἀπόστολοι; μὴ πάντες προφῆται; μὴ πάντες διδάσκαλοι; μὴ πάντες δυνάμεις;
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
μὴ πάντες χαρίσματα ἔχουσιν ἰαμάτων; μὴ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλοῦσιν; μὴ πάντες διερμηνεύουσιν;
But earnestly desire the greater gifts.[^17] And I will show you a still more excellent way.
ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα. καὶ ἔτι καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι.

n.1: Or "spiritual people". Greek *pneumatika* or *pneumatikoi*; the form used can mean either.
n.2: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike (see 1:10).
n.4: The Greek is difficult; literally "how you were led, being carried away". Some interpreters see a reference to frenzied experiences in pagan worship.
n.6: Greek *charismata*, "gifts of grace" (see 1:7); also in verses 9, 28, 30 and 31.
n.8: Literally "a word of wisdom"; and "a word of knowledge".
n.10: Greek *propheteia*, speaking a message from God. In chapter 14 it is speech in the gathered church that others can understand, which builds up, encourages and comforts (14:3) and can lay bare the secrets of the heart (14:24–25), and which others are to weigh (14:29). How far it included prediction is discussed.
n.11: Literally "discernments of spirits", probably the ability to judge whether an utterance comes from the Spirit of God or from another spirit. Compare 14:29.
n.12: Greek *glossai*, "tongues, languages"; also in verses 28 and 30. Paul describes speech that others cannot understand unless it is interpreted (14:2–28). Whether he means human languages unknown to the speaker (compare Acts 2:4–11) or speech that is not any human language (compare 13:1, "the tongues of angels") is debated.
n.14: That is, the private parts of the body.
n.15: Greek *antilempseis*, "forms of help", and *kyberneseis*, "forms of guidance", literally "steering", as by a ship's pilot.
n.17: Or "But you are eagerly seeking the greater gifts", a statement rather than a command. Many manuscripts read "the better gifts".

v: If I speak in the tongues[^1] of human beings and of angels, but do not have love,[^2] I have become a noisy gong[^3] or a clanging cymbal.
Ἐὰν ταῖς γλώσσαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαλῶ καὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον ἀλαλάζον.
And if I have prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to move mountains,[^4] but do not have love, I am nothing.
καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω προφητείαν καὶ εἰδῶ τὰ μυστήρια πάντα καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γνῶσιν, καὶ ἐὰν ἔχω πᾶσαν τὴν πίστιν ὥστε ὄρη μεθιστάναι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐθέν εἰμι.
And if I give away all my possessions to feed others,[^5] and if I hand over my body so that I may be burned,[^6] but do not have love, I gain nothing.
καὶ ἐὰν ψωμίσω πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντά μου, καὶ ἐὰν παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου, ἵνα καυθήσομαι, ἀγάπην δὲ μὴ ἔχω, οὐδὲν ὠφελοῦμαι.
Love is patient, love is kind. Love is not jealous, it does not brag, it is not puffed up,[^7]
Ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ, χρηστεύεται ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ ζηλοῖ ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐ περπερεύεται, οὐ φυσιοῦται,
it does not behave improperly, it does not seek its own interests, it is not easily angered, it does not keep a record of wrongs,[^8]
οὐκ ἀσχημονεῖ, οὐ ζητεῖ τὰ ἑαυτῆς, οὐ παροξύνεται, οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν,
it does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices with the truth.
οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ, συγχαίρει δὲ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·
It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.[^9]
πάντα στέγει, πάντα πιστεύει, πάντα ἐλπίζει, πάντα ὑπομένει.
Love never fails.[^10] But as for prophecies, they will be brought to an end;[^11] as for tongues, they will cease; as for knowledge, it will be brought to an end.
Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε πίπτει. εἴτε δὲ προφητεῖαι, καταργηθήσονται· εἴτε γλῶσσαι, παύσονται· εἴτε γνῶσις, καταργηθήσεται.
For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
ἐκ μέρους γὰρ γινώσκομεν καὶ ἐκ μέρους προφητεύομεν·
but when what is complete[^12] comes, what is in part will be brought to an end.
ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ τὸ τέλειον, τὸ ἐκ μέρους καταργηθήσεται.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put an end to childish ways.
ὅτε ἤμην νήπιος, ἐλάλουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐφρόνουν ὡς νήπιος, ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος· ὅτε γέγονα ἀνήρ, κατήργηκα τὰ τοῦ νηπίου.
For now we see in a mirror, dimly,[^13] but then face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, even as I have been fully known.
βλέπομεν γὰρ ἄρτι διʼ ἐσόπτρου ἐν αἰνίγματι, τότε δὲ πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον· ἄρτι γινώσκω ἐκ μέρους, τότε δὲ ἐπιγνώσομαι καθὼς καὶ ἐπεγνώσθην.
So now faith, hope and love remain, these three; but the greatest[^14] of these is love.
νυνὶ δὲ μένει πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀγάπη· τὰ τρία ταῦτα, μείζων δὲ τούτων ἡ ἀγάπη.

n.5: Or "If I dole out all my possessions". Greek *psomizo*, "feed by putting bits of food into the mouth".
n.6: Some manuscripts read "so that I may boast".
n.8: Literally "it does not reckon the evil".
n.9: Or "It always bears, always believes, always hopes, always endures." *Bears*: or "covers", "protects".
n.11: Greek *katargeo* (see 1:28); also later in this verse and in verses 10 and 11 ("put an end to").
n.12: Greek *teleion*, "complete, perfect, mature" (compare 2:6). What it refers to is debated. Most interpreters think of the end of the age, when believers will see "face to face" (verse 12); others think of a mature state of the church, or of the completed scriptures.
n.13: Literally "through a mirror in a riddle". Mirrors were made of polished metal and gave an imperfect image. Compare Numbers 12:8, where Yahweh speaks with Moses "face to face, plainly and not in riddles".

v: Pursue love, and earnestly desire spiritual gifts,[^1] but especially that you may prophesy.[^2]
Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην, ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε.
For one who speaks in a tongue[^3] does not speak to people but to God, for no one understands him;[^4] he speaks mysteries in the Spirit.[^5]
ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ ἀλλὰ θεῷ, οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀκούει, πνεύματι δὲ λαλεῖ μυστήρια·
But one who prophesies speaks to people for their building up, encouragement and comfort.
ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ παράκλησιν καὶ παραμυθίαν.
One who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, but one who prophesies builds up the church.
ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ· ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ.
I would like all of you to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. One who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets,[^6] so that the church may be built up.
θέλω δὲ πάντας ὑμᾶς λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε· μείζων δὲ ὁ προφητεύων ἢ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ διερμηνεύῃ, ἵνα ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβῃ.
Now, brothers and sisters,[^7] if I come to you speaking in tongues, what good will I do you unless I speak to you with some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
Νῦν δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς γλώσσαις λαλῶν, τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω, ἐὰν μὴ ὑμῖν λαλήσω ἢ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει ἢ ἐν γνώσει ἢ ἐν προφητείᾳ ἢ ἐν διδαχῇ;
In the same way, lifeless instruments that produce sound, such as the flute or the harp, if they do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is being played on the flute or the harp?
ὅμως τὰ ἄψυχα φωνὴν διδόντα, εἴτε αὐλὸς εἴτε κιθάρα, ἐὰν διαστολὴν τοῖς φθόγγοις μὴ δῷ, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον;
And if the trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will get ready for battle?
καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἄδηλον φωνὴν σάλπιγξ δῷ, τίς παρασκευάσεται εἰς πόλεμον;
So it is with you: if with your tongue you do not speak intelligible words, how will anyone know what is being said? You will be speaking into the air.
οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς διὰ τῆς γλώσσης ἐὰν μὴ εὔσημον λόγον δῶτε, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ λαλούμενον; ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες.
There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages[^8] in the world, and none is without meaning.
τοσαῦτα εἰ τύχοι γένη φωνῶν εἰσιν ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ οὐδὲν ἄφωνον·
If then I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner[^9] to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.
ἐὰν οὖν μὴ εἰδῶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς φωνῆς, ἔσομαι τῷ λαλοῦντι βάρβαρος καὶ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν ἐμοὶ βάρβαρος.
So it is with you: since you are eager for spirits,[^10] seek to excel in them for the building up of the church.
οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ἐπεὶ ζηλωταί ἐστε πνευμάτων, πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ζητεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε.
Therefore one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
Διὸ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ προσευχέσθω ἵνα διερμηνεύῃ.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays,[^11] but my mind is unproductive.[^12]
ἐὰν γὰρ προσεύχωμαι γλώσσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμά μου προσεύχεται, ὁ δὲ νοῦς μου ἄκαρπός ἐστιν.
What then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind. I will sing praise with the spirit, and I will also sing praise with the mind.
τί οὖν ἐστιν; προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι, προσεύξομαι δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ· ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι, ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ·
Otherwise, if you give a blessing with the spirit, how can anyone in the position of an outsider[^13] say "Amen"[^14] to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
ἐπεὶ ἐὰν εὐλογῇς πνεύματι, ὁ ἀναπληρῶν τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἰδιώτου πῶς ἐρεῖ τὸ Ἀμήν ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ; ἐπειδὴ τί λέγεις οὐκ οἶδεν·
For you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
σὺ μὲν γὰρ καλῶς εὐχαριστεῖς, ἀλλʼ ὁ ἕτερος οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖται.
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ, πάντων ὑμῶν μᾶλλον γλώσσαις λαλῶ·
But in church I would rather speak five words with my mind, in order to instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ θέλω πέντε λόγους τῷ νοΐ μου λαλῆσαι, ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους κατηχήσω, ἢ μυρίους λόγους ἐν γλώσσῃ.
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature.
Ἀδελφοί, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶν τέλειοι γίνεσθε.
In the Law it is written, "By people of other tongues and by the lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord."[^15]
ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι Ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέρων λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ οὐδʼ οὕτως εἰσακούσονταί μου, λέγει κύριος.
So then, tongues are a sign[^16] not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις, ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.
So if the whole church comes together in one place and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες λαλῶσιν γλώσσαις, εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι, οὐκ ἐροῦσιν ὅτι μαίνεσθε;
But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider comes in, he is convicted by all and examined by all,
ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύωσιν, εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης, ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων,
the secrets of his heart are laid bare, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God and declare, "God is really among you!"[^17]
τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ φανερὰ γίνεται, καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ θεῷ, ἀπαγγέλλων ὅτι Ὄντως ὁ θεὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
What then, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each one has a psalm,[^18] a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Let everything be done for building up.
Τί οὖν ἐστιν, ἀδελφοί; ὅταν συνέρχησθε, ἕκαστος ψαλμὸν ἔχει, διδαχὴν ἔχει, ἀποκάλυψιν ἔχει, γλῶσσαν ἔχει, ἑρμηνείαν ἔχει· πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two or at most three, each in turn, and let someone interpret.
εἴτε γλώσσῃ τις λαλεῖ, κατὰ δύο ἢ τὸ πλεῖστον τρεῖς, καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος, καὶ εἷς διερμηνευέτω·
But if there is no interpreter, let each of them keep silent in the church and speak to himself and to God.
ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ διερμηνευτής, σιγάτω ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαλείτω καὶ τῷ θεῷ.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said.[^19]
προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι διακρινέτωσαν·
If a revelation comes to someone else who is sitting there, the first should be silent.
ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω.
For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged
δύνασθε γὰρ καθʼ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν, ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται
(and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets,
(καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται,
for God is not a God of disorder but of peace), as in all the churches of God's holy people.[^20]
οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης), ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων.
The women[^21] should keep silent in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the Law also says.[^22]
Αἱ γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις σιγάτωσαν, οὐ γὰρ ἐπιτρέπεται αὐταῖς λαλεῖν· ἀλλὰ ὑποτασσέσθωσαν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ νόμος λέγει.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
εἰ δέ τι μαθεῖν θέλουσιν, ἐν οἴκῳ τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας ἐπερωτάτωσαν, αἰσχρὸν γάρ ἐστιν γυναικὶ λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ.
Or did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
ἢ ἀφʼ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν, ἢ εἰς ὑμᾶς μόνους κατήντησεν;
If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, he should acknowledge that what I am writing to you is the Lord's.[^23]
Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι ἢ πνευματικός, ἐπιγινωσκέτω ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν ὅτι κυρίου ἐστίν·
If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.[^24]
εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ, ἀγνοεῖται.
So, my brothers and sisters, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν, καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν μὴ κωλύετε γλώσσαις·
But everything should be done decently and in order.
πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω.

n.2: Greek *propheteuo*, "speak as a prophet" (see 12:10); so throughout the chapter.
n.3: Or "in a language". Greek *glossa* (see 12:10); so throughout the chapter.
n.7: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike (see 1:10); also in verses 20, 26 and 39.
n.8: Literally "voices" or "sounds", Greek *phonai*, not the word used for "tongues". *None is without meaning*: literally "none is voiceless".
n.9: Greek *barbaros*, someone whose speech sounds like meaningless noise, a speaker of a foreign language.
n.10: Literally "zealous for spirits", probably meaning spiritual gifts or manifestations of the Spirit.
n.11: Or "the Spirit in me prays". So also "with the spirit" in verses 15 and 16.
n.13: Greek *idiotes*, an ordinary person without special knowledge or skill; also in verses 23 and 24. Here perhaps someone who is enquiring, or a believer who does not understand tongues.
n.14: A Hebrew word meaning "it is firm, it is true", said to affirm a prayer.
n.15: Isaiah 28:11–12, in a form that differs from both the Hebrew and the Septuagint; the words "says the Lord" are not in Isaiah. In Isaiah, Yahweh will speak to his people through the foreign speech of invaders, a people who "would not listen". Here "the Law" means the scriptures as a whole.
n.16: The sense of "sign" here is debated. In the light of verse 21, tongues may be a sign of judgment on those who do not believe; verses 23–25 describe the effect of each gift on unbelievers.
n.19: Greek *diakrino*, "discern, evaluate" (compare 11:29 and 12:10). "The others" may be the other prophets or the whole church.
n.20: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "saints". The SBLGNT's punctuation joins "as in all the churches of God's holy people" to what comes before. Many translations begin verse 34 with it: "As in all the churches of the saints, the women should keep silent …"
n.21: Or "wives". Greek *gynaikes*, "women, wives" (compare "their own husbands", verse 35). Many manuscripts read "Your women". Verses 34–35 are much discussed. In a few manuscripts, mainly of the Western text (the Greek-Latin Codices Claromontanus, Augiensis and Boernerianus, known as D, F and G, the minuscule 88 and some Latin witnesses), they stand after verse 40. The SBLGNT apparatus, which compares printed editions, does not record this, and all the editions it compares print the verses here. Some scholars think the verses began as a note in the margin that was copied into the text at two different places; others hold that Paul wrote them here. Since 11:5 assumes that women pray and prophesy, interpreters who take the verses as Paul's understand the silence in different ways: for example, as a limit on asking questions during worship, on speech that disrupts it, or on weighing the prophecies (verse 29). Some read verses 34–35 as a view held in Corinth, which Paul rejects in verse 36.
n.22: The passage of the Law is not named. Genesis 3:16 is often suggested.
n.23: The SBLGNT reads "is the Lord's". Most editions read "is the Lord's command", and many manuscripts "are the Lord's commands".
n.24: That is, by God. Many manuscripts read "If anyone is ignorant of this, let him remain ignorant."

v: Now I want to remind you,[^1] brothers and sisters,[^2] of the good news that I proclaimed to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε, ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἑστήκατε,
through which you are also being saved, if you hold firmly to the message I proclaimed to you,[^3] unless you believed in vain.
διʼ οὗ καὶ σῴζεσθε, τίνι λόγῳ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, εἰ κατέχετε, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε.
For I handed on to you as of first importance[^4] what I also received:[^5] that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the scriptures,[^6]
Παρέδωκα γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν πρώτοις, ὃ καὶ παρέλαβον, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
that he was buried, that he was raised[^7] on the third day in accordance with the scriptures,
καὶ ὅτι ἐτάφη, καὶ ὅτι ἐγήγερται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
and that he appeared[^8] to Cephas,[^9] then to the Twelve.
καὶ ὅτι ὤφθη Κηφᾷ, εἶτα τοῖς δώδεκα·
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep.[^10]
ἔπειτα ὤφθη ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐφάπαξ, ἐξ ὧν οἱ πλείονες μένουσιν ἕως ἄρτι, τινὲς δὲ ἐκοιμήθησαν·
Then he appeared to James,[^11] then to all the apostles.
ἔπειτα ὤφθη Ἰακώβῳ, εἶτα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πᾶσιν·
Last of all, as to one untimely born,[^12] he appeared to me also.
ἔσχατον δὲ πάντων ὡσπερεὶ τῷ ἐκτρώματι ὤφθη κἀμοί.
For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ἐλάχιστος τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὃς οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς καλεῖσθαι ἀπόστολος, διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ·
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
χάριτι δὲ θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι, καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη, ἀλλὰ περισσότερον αὐτῶν πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ σὺν ἐμοί.
Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we proclaim and this is what you believed.
εἴτε οὖν ἐγὼ εἴτε ἐκεῖνοι, οὕτως κηρύσσομεν καὶ οὕτως ἐπιστεύσατε.
Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
Εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς κηρύσσεται ὅτι ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγήγερται, πῶς λέγουσιν ἐν ὑμῖν τινες ὅτι ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν;
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
εἰ δὲ ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty and your faith[^13] is empty too.
εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, κενὸν ἄρα τὸ κήρυγμα ἡμῶν, κενὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν,
We are even found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified about God[^14] that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if in fact the dead are not raised.
εὑρισκόμεθα δὲ καὶ ψευδομάρτυρες τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐμαρτυρήσαμεν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι ἤγειρεν τὸν Χριστόν, ὃν οὐκ ἤγειρεν εἴπερ ἄρα νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται.
For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised.
εἰ γὰρ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, ματαία ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, ἔτι ἐστὲ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν.
Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο.
If only for this life we have hoped in Christ,[^15] we are of all people most to be pitied.
εἰ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμὲν μόνον, ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits[^16] of those who have fallen asleep.
Νυνὶ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων.
For since death came through a human being, the resurrection of the dead has also come through a human being.
ἐπειδὴ γὰρ διʼ ἀνθρώπου θάνατος, καὶ διʼ ἀνθρώπου ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν·
For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνῄσκουσιν, οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ πάντες ζῳοποιηθήσονται.
But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then at his coming[^17] those who belong to Christ.
ἕκαστος δὲ ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι· ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός, ἔπειτα οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ·
Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after he has brought to nothing[^18] every ruler and every authority and power.
εἶτα τὸ τέλος, ὅταν παραδιδῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί, ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν,
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.[^19]
δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρι οὗ θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ.
The last enemy to be brought to nothing is death.
ἔσχατος ἐχθρὸς καταργεῖται ὁ θάνατος,
For "he has put everything under his feet."[^20] But when it says,[^21] "Everything has been put under him," it is clear that this does not include the one who put everything under him.
πάντα γὰρ ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ ὅτι πάντα ὑποτέτακται, δῆλον ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα.
When everything has been put under him, then the Son himself will be put under[^22] the one who put everything under him, so that God may be all in all.
ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, τότε αὐτὸς ὁ υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ᾖ ὁ θεὸς πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
Otherwise, what will those people do who are baptized on behalf of the dead?[^23] If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized on their behalf?
Ἐπεὶ τί ποιήσουσιν οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν; εἰ ὅλως νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, τί καὶ βαπτίζονται ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν;
And why are we in danger every hour?
τί καὶ ἡμεῖς κινδυνεύομεν πᾶσαν ὥραν;
I die every day! That is as sure as my boasting about you,[^24] which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω, νὴ τὴν ὑμετέραν καύχησιν, ἣν ἔχω ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
If, from a merely human point of view,[^25] I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus,[^26] what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."[^27]
εἰ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος; εἰ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, Φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν, αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκομεν.
Do not be deceived: "Bad company corrupts good character."[^28]
μὴ πλανᾶσθε· φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί.
Wake up and be sober, as is right, and stop sinning. For some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
ἐκνήψατε δικαίως καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε, ἀγνωσίαν γὰρ θεοῦ τινες ἔχουσιν· πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λαλῶ.
But someone will ask, "How are the dead raised? With what kind of body do they come?"
Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις· Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί, ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται;
You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
ἄφρων, σὺ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ ζῳοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·
And what you sow is not the body that is to be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or of something else.
καὶ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν·
But God gives it a body as he has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body.
ὁ δὲ θεὸς δίδωσιν αὐτῷ σῶμα καθὼς ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπερμάτων ἴδιον σῶμα.
Not all flesh is the same: human beings have one kind of flesh, animals another, birds another, and fish another.
οὐ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἡ αὐτὴ σάρξ, ἀλλὰ ἄλλη μὲν ἀνθρώπων, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων.
There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory[^29] of the heavenly is one kind and the glory of the earthly is another.
καὶ σώματα ἐπουράνια, καὶ σώματα ἐπίγεια· ἀλλὰ ἑτέρα μὲν ἡ τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξα, ἑτέρα δὲ ἡ τῶν ἐπιγείων.
There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.
ἄλλη δόξα ἡλίου, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα σελήνης, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα ἀστέρων, ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in decay; it is raised imperishable.
Οὕτως καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν. σπείρεται ἐν φθορᾷ, ἐγείρεται ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ·
It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
σπείρεται ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ· σπείρεται ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δυνάμει·
It is sown a natural body;[^30] it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.[^31]
σπείρεται σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἐγείρεται σῶμα πνευματικόν. Εἰ ἔστιν σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἔστιν καὶ πνευματικόν.
So also it is written, "The first man, Adam, became a living being";[^32] the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
οὕτως καὶ γέγραπται· Ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν· ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζῳοποιοῦν.
But it is not the spiritual that comes first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
ἀλλʼ οὐ πρῶτον τὸ πνευματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ψυχικόν, ἔπειτα τὸ πνευματικόν.
The first man was from the earth, made of dust;[^33] the second man is from heaven.[^34]
ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός, ὁ δεύτερος ἄνθρωπος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ.
As was the man of dust, so are those who are of the dust; and as is the man of heaven, so are those who are of heaven.
οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι·
And just as we have borne the image of the man of dust, we will also bear[^35] the image of the man of heaven.
καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.
What I mean, brothers and sisters, is this: flesh and blood[^36] cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does decay inherit what is imperishable.
Τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ δύναται, οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ.
Listen, I tell you a mystery: we will not all fall asleep, but we will all be changed,
ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα,
in a moment, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.
For this perishable body must put on the imperishable, and this mortal body must put on immortality.[^37]
δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.
When this perishable body puts on the imperishable, and this mortal body puts on immortality,[^38] then the saying that is written will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."[^39]
ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος· Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.
"Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?"[^40]
ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ νῖκος; ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον;
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the Law.
τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
So, my dear brothers and sisters, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί, ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι, περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ κυρίου πάντοτε, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν κυρίῳ.

n.2: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike (see 1:10); also in verses 6, 50 and 58.
n.3: The Greek is compressed; literally "with what word I proclaimed it to you, if you hold it fast".
n.5: "Handed on" and "received" are the usual words for passing on a tradition (see 11:23). Many scholars think that in verses 3–5, and perhaps beyond, Paul is quoting an early summary of the faith that he had been taught, with its repeated "that". Where the quoted words end is debated; the list of appearances in verses 6–8 may be Paul's own addition, at least in part, and verse 6 has his comment "most of whom are still alive".
n.6: No passage is named, here or in verse 4. Isaiah 53:5–12 is often suggested for Christ's death "for our sins", and Hosea 6:2 for "on the third day".
n.7: The Greek perfect tense, "has been raised", which stresses that he remains raised. So throughout the chapter.
n.8: Literally "was seen by"; so also in verses 6–8.
n.10: That is, have died; also in verses 18, 20 and 51.
n.11: Probably James the brother of the Lord (Galatians 1:19; compare Mark 6:3).
n.12: Greek *ektroma*, "a miscarriage", a child born dead or before its time. It may have been a term of abuse used against Paul, or a picture of his sudden and abnormal "birth" as an apostle.
n.15: Or "If in this life we have only hoped in Christ".
n.16: The first part of the harvest, offered to God (Leviticus 23:10), a pledge of the rest to come; also in verse 23.
n.17: Greek *parousia*, "presence, arrival", a word also used of the visit of a ruler.
n.18: Greek *katargeo* (see 1:28); also in verse 26. *Ruler … authority … power*: these may be spiritual powers (compare 2:6).
n.22: Or "will subject himself to". Greek *hypotasso*, the verb translated "put under" throughout verses 27–28. Many manuscripts read "then the Son himself also".
n.23: Baptism "on behalf of the dead" is not mentioned anywhere else in the New Testament or in other early Christian writings, and its meaning is unknown. Many explanations have been proposed: for example, that some believers were baptized in place of people who had died without being baptized; that people were baptized for the sake of believers who had died, hoping to be reunited with them; or that the phrase refers to being baptized in view of one's own death. Greek *hyper*, "for, on behalf of, for the sake of".
n.24: Literally "by your boasting", an oath formula: Paul swears by his pride in them. The SBLGNT here follows the Byzantine text; other editions add "brothers and sisters".
n.25: Literally "according to a human being". It may mean "with merely human hopes", or "speaking in human terms".
n.26: This may be a figure of speech for fierce opponents, or refer to a real danger in the arena.
n.28: A line from the Greek comic poet Menander (4th century BC), in his play *Thais*, which had become a proverb.
n.29: Greek *doxa*, "glory, splendor, brightness"; also in verse 41.
n.30: Greek *psychikos* (see 2:14), from *psyche*, the word translated "being" in verse 45; also in verse 46.
n.31: Many manuscripts read "There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body."
n.32: Genesis 2:7, with "first" and "Adam" added. *Living being*: Greek *psyche zosa*, translating the Hebrew *nephesh chayyah*.
n.33: Compare Genesis 2:7, "from the dust of the ground".
n.34: Many manuscripts read "the second man is the Lord from heaven".
n.35: The SBLGNT here follows NA28; other editions read "let us also bear". The two Greek forms differ by one letter.
n.36: That is, human beings in their present, mortal state.
n.37: Literally "this perishable", "this mortal"; also in verse 54.
n.38: Some manuscripts leave out "this perishable body puts on the imperishable, and".
n.39: Isaiah 25:8. The Hebrew reads "He will swallow up death forever"; the word translated "forever", *lanetsach*, can also mean "in victory". Paul's wording differs from the Septuagint and agrees with the later Greek translation of Theodotion.
n.40: Hosea 13:14, adapted from the Septuagint, which has "Where is your penalty, O death? Where is your sting, O Hades?" The Hebrew reads "Where, O death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your destruction?" Many manuscripts read "Where, O death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory?" *Hades*: the realm of the dead, like Sheol.

v: Now concerning the collection for God's holy people:[^1] you should do what I directed the churches of Galatia to do.
Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογείας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους, ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε.
On the first day of every week,[^2] each of you is to put something aside and save it up, as he may prosper, so that collections will not have to be made when I come.
κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρʼ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ τι ἐὰν εὐοδῶται, ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογεῖαι γίνωνται.
When I arrive, I will send those whom you approve with letters[^3] to take your gift[^4] to Jerusalem.
ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι, οὓς ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε διʼ ἐπιστολῶν, τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ·
If it is fitting for me to go too, they will go with me.
ἐὰν δὲ ἄξιον ᾖ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι, σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται.
I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω, Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι,
Perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way, wherever I go.
πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν παραμενῶ ἢ καὶ παραχειμάσω, ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι.
For I do not want to see you now just in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος ἐπιτρέψῃ.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,[^5]
ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς πεντηκοστῆς·
for a wide and effective door has opened to me, and there are many who oppose me.
θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής, καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί.
If Timothy comes, see that he has nothing to fear among you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, as I am.
Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος, βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τὸ γὰρ ἔργον κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς κἀγώ·
So let no one despise him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.[^6]
μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ. προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ, ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός με, ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
Now concerning our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his will[^7] to come now. He will come when he has the opportunity.
Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν· καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ, ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ.
Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, be courageous,[^8] be strong.
Γρηγορεῖτε, στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε.
Let all that you do be done in love.
πάντα ὑμῶν ἐν ἀγάπῃ γινέσθω.
Now I urge you, brothers and sisters[^9] (you know that the household of Stephanas were the first converts in Achaia,[^10] and that they have devoted themselves to serving God's holy people),
Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί· οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς·
to submit to such people, and to everyone who works with them and labors.
ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι.
I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus have come, because they have made up for your absence,[^11]
χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ, ὅτι τὸ ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν,
for they refreshed my spirit and yours. So give recognition to such people.
ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν. ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους.
The churches of Asia[^12] send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca,[^13] together with the church in their house, send you warm greetings in the Lord.
Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας. ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατʼ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.
All the brothers and sisters send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες. ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.[^14]
Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be cursed![^15] Marana tha![^16]
εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν κύριον, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα. Μαράνα θά.
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus.[^17]
ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

n.1: Literally "the holy ones", traditionally "saints"; also in verse 15. Here the believers in Jerusalem (verse 3; compare Romans 15:25–26).
n.2: Literally "on one of the Sabbath", an expression for the first day of the week (compare Mark 16:2).
n.3: Or "whomever you approve, I will send with letters". The Greek can be read either way.
n.4: Literally "your grace". Greek *charis*, here a gift given freely.
n.5: Greek *pentekoste*, "fiftieth": the Jewish Festival of Weeks, fifty days after Passover (Leviticus 23:15–21; Deuteronomy 16:9–12).
n.6: Greek *adelphoi*, probably fellow workers traveling with Timothy; also in verse 12. Or "with the brothers and sisters".
n.7: Or "it was not at all God's will". Literally "it was not at all will".
n.9: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike (see 1:10); also in verse 20.
n.10: Literally "the firstfruits of Achaia" (see 15:20). Achaia was the Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital.
n.11: Or "they have supplied what you lacked". Literally "they have filled up your lack".
n.12: The Roman province of Asia, with Ephesus as its chief city.
n.13: Called Priscilla in Acts 18:2, 18 and 26. Many manuscripts read "Priscilla" here.
n.14: Paul usually dictated his letters to a scribe (compare Romans 16:22) and added a closing greeting in his own handwriting (compare Galatians 6:11).
n.16: An Aramaic phrase. As divided in the SBLGNT, following NA28, it means "Our Lord, come!" (compare Revelation 22:20). The other editions divide the letters differently, *maran atha*, "Our Lord has come" or "Our Lord is coming".
